intro: Spirit landed in Gusev Crater on January 4, 2004 — three weeks before its twin Opportunity touched down on the opposite side of Mars. Designed for 90 sols, Spirit operated for 6 years and traversed 7.7 km until its wheels became permanently mired in soft soil at "Troy". From a stranded rover, it continued as a stationary science platform until contact was lost in March 2010.

images.caption: Mars Exploration Rover during integration — 185 kg, 6 wheels, Pancam mast camera, RAT rock-abrasion tool.
Winter Haven at McMurdo, sols 814-980 (2006) — Pancam 360° panorama. The Columbia Hills, named for the lost STS-107 crew, dominate the horizon.
Spirit's Troy stuck-rover site, captured by MRO HiRISE after wheel embedment in May 2009.
Drilling at the Adirondack rock, sol 34 — first use of the rock-abrasion tool on Mars.
